MINUTES
  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  MONDAY, APRIL 1, 2024

A regular meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order by VICE CHAIR OLSON at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chamber.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI led those assembled in the Pledge of Allegiance.

3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Olson, Nicklas, Repp-Loadsman, Romanelli, Schachter, Yoo

  Commissioners Absent:  Medawar

  Staff Present:  Jeannie Naughton, Community Development Director
  Whitney Berry, Senior Planner
  Katrina Kawagoe, Assistant Planner
  Carol Corea, Administrative Analyst

4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES, MARCH 4, 2024

COMMISSIONER YOO, seconded by COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN to,

  APPROVE THE PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES OF MARCH 4, 2024.

There being no objection, VICE CHAIR OLSON so ordered.

5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

NONE

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

A.  READING IN FULL OF ALL ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS PRESENTED FOR
  CONSIDERATION TO THE PLANNING COMMISSION WILL BE WAIVED AND ALL
  SUCH ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS WILL BE READ BY TITLE ONLY.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  APPROVE ITEM 6A

There being no objection, VICE CHAIR OLSON so ordered.

7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-230269; ADDRESS: 30 Club View Lane, Rolling Hills
  Estates, CA 90274; APPLICANT: Werner Toledo, Maclary Design; A request for a
  Neighborhood Compatibility Determination (NC-230270) for a 323 square foot addition,
  including 112 square feet (SF) first floor addition and a 211 SF second floor addition, to
  an existing two-story single-family residence.

Senior Planner Berry provided a presentation for Planning Application No. PA-230269,
summarizing the staff report. This proposal requires Neighborhood Compatibility Determination
and staff found that all five criteria were met.

Senior Planner Berry stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission approve
Planning Application No. PA-230269, subject to the conditions outlined in the staff report.

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, APRIL 1, 2024
  1
 VICE CHAIR OLSON asked for any questions or comments in favor or in opposition of the project.
There were no questions or comments.

VICE CHAIR OLSON recommended that the Holiday decorations be removed.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  APPROVE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-230269,  SUBJECT  TO  THE
  CONDITIONS OUTLINED IN THE STAFF REPORT.

AYES: Olson, Nicklas, Repp-Loadsman, Romanelli, Schachter, Yoo
NOES:
ABSENT: Medawar
ABSTAIN:

Director Naughton stated that the Planning Commission has approved Planning Application No.
PA-230269, A request for a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination for a 323 square foot
addition, including 112 SF first floor addition and a 211 SF second floor addition, to an existing
two-story single-family residence. There is a 20-day appeal period for any member of the public
and the City Council by its own motion.

Items taken out of order.

8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-240078; ADDRESS: 12 Sorrel Lane, Rolling Hills
  Estates, CA 90274; APPLICANT: Luis de Moraes; A request for a Neighborhood
  Compatibility Determination (NC-240079) for the 3,131 square foot two-story addition to
  an existing single-story residence; and a request for a Variance (V-240080) to legalize the
  existing nonconforming side yard setbacks.

Assistant Planner Kawagoe provided a presentation for Planning Application No. PA-240078
summarizing the staff report. This proposal requires a Variance and staff found that all five findings
to support the Variance were met. The Dappplegray Lanes Property Owners Association provided
staff with additional Conditions of Approval for the project; staff is in agreement with the conditions
and these will be added to the resolution.

Assistant Planner Kawagoe stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission: open
the public hearing; take public testimony; discuss the issues; close the public hearing, and adopt
Resolution No. PA-240078, approving the project.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING.

There being no objection VICE CHAIR OLSON so ordered.

COMMISSIONER YOO asked if any comments were received from the neighbors. Assistant
Planner Kawagoe stated that a question regarding the distance the proposed project will be from
the side yard setback; however, there were no objections or additional comments received by
staff.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN inquired about the distance of the window, that is being
installed for the new bedroom/massage room, to the wall, which is proposed in the side yard
setback.

Luis de Moraes, Architect, explained that there will be a window well on the lower level and there
will be an escape ladder from the upper level, which is required by code for egress.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER inquired about concerns about water issues with the bridle trail
and if this has been addressed. Mr. Moraes stated that he has not had time to investigate the
issues (DLPOA sent additional conditions of approval shortly before the meeting) and will work
with staff to resolve this.

Associate Planner Berry stated that staff will be including two of the conditions of approval
submitted by the DLPOA, which are: 1) that the rear yard fence will be moved outside of the bridle
trail easement; 2) a recommendation to provide planning with documentation on the installation
of drainage in the rear of the property.

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, APRIL 1, 2024
  2
 COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked about the neighbor approvals. Assistant Planner Kawagoe
stated that as a condition of approval, the applicant will provide staff with the plans signed by the
adjoining neighbors.

Director Naughton stated that for over the counter or administrative approvals, it was customary
for the neighbors to review and sign the plans; however, for this application notices were mailed,
and this was a published agenda item; neighbors had ample time to object to the project prior and
at this meeting. Director Naughton stated that she does not recommend adding neighbor
signatures on the plans as a condition of approval.

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN, Senior Planner Berry stated
that the last DLPOA condition of approval regarding the drainage is an area that will be handled
through the building and safety process. The recommendation is that a condition is added for the
applicant to provide documentation on the drainage installation.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER requested that construction access is limited to the front of the
property to avoid any issues with the bridle trail users.

VICE CHAIR OLSON requested that the area for trash receptacles is added to the plans.

VICE CHAIR OLSON expressed concern with the hardscape and asked if there was any way to
minimize the visual impact. Mr. Moraes stated that the front yard was paved as part of an earlier
project in an effort to guide water due to drainage issues on the property. The driveway to the
garage is original to the property. Mr. Moraes stated that he would need to discuss this with a civil
engineer to see if there are other alternatives to having the area paved.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING.

There being no objection VICE CHAIR OLSON so ordered.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
SCHACTHER to,

  APPROVE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-240078 WITH THE CONDITIONS
  OUTLINED IN THE STAFF REPORT AND ADDITIONAL CONDITIONS, AS FOLLOWS:
  1) A DRAINAGE PLAN BE SUBMITTED TO BUILDING AND SAFETY THAT ADDRESS
  ALL ON-SITE AND OFF-SITE CONDITIONS; 2) THAT THE REAR YARD FENCE DOES
  NOT ENCROACH INTO THE BRIDLE TRAIL; 3) CONSTRUCTION ACCESS IS TO BE
  LIMITED TO THE FRONT OF THE PROPERTY AND NO ACCESS THROUGH THE
  BRIDLE TRAIL; AND 4) THAT THE PLANS ARE REVISED TO SHOW THE LOCATION
  OF TRASH RECEPTACLES.

AYES: Olson, Nicklas, Repp-Loadsman, Romanelli, Schachter, Yoo
NOES:
ABSENT: Medawar
ABSTAIN:

Director Naughton stated that the Planning Commission has approved Resolution No. PA-
240078, a request for a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination for the 3,131 square foot two-
story addition to an existing single-story residence; and a request for a Variance to legalize the
existing nonconforming side yard setbacks at 12 Sorrel Lane. There is a 20-day appeal period
for any member of the public and the City Council by its own motion.

B.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-240067; ADDRESS: 20 Palos Verdes Drive Lane,
  Rolling Hills Estates, CA 90274; APPLICANT: Bharat Chhabra; A request for a
  Neighborhood Compatibility Determination (NC-240068) for the 750 square foot second
  story Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) above an existing garage; and a request for a
  Variance (V-240110) for the structural alterations to the existing garage, that maintain a
  nonconforming rear yard setback, to allow for the construction of a second story ADU.

Assistant Planner Kawagoe provided a presentation for Planning Application No. PA-240067
summarizing the staff report. The proposed project is to construct 750 SF ADU above an existing
garage and bedroom. A Neighborhood Compatibility Determination is required for any second
story addition. The roof ridge height is increasing from 17’-5” to 22’-6”; to minimize the impact of
the privacy of the neighbor to the north, two clerestory windows were placed on that side.

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, APRIL 1, 2024
  3
 Assistant Planner stated that staff received two letters of opposition of this project with concerns
related to privacy and view impacts. Privacy will not be impacted since the ADU will be significantly
setback from the property lines from both sides of the property. Views will also be minimally
impacted; in addition, the City’s policy does not address the preservation of neighboring trees or
vegetation or blue skies. Staff determined that this project is not in violation of the City’s View
Ordinance. A variance is also required to maintain a non-conforming rear yard setback for the
structural alterations to the first floor to allow for the construction of the ADU; staff determined that
all five findings to support the Variance were met.

Assistant Planner Kawagoe stated that State laws allow ADUs by right, however, the city's code
requires Neighborhood Compatibility Determination for the second story addition and two-story
ADUs. Therefore, the purview of the Commission is limited to bulk and mass design and privacy
related to the proposed second story construction.

Assistant Planner Kawagoe stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission open
the public hearing; take public testimony; discuss the issues; and close the public hearing and
adopt resolution number, PA-240067 approving the project.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN inquired about the floor plan, which indicates that there will
be a balcony off the bedroom and asked if it had been removed since the elevations indicate only
windows. Assistant Planner Kawagoe stated that she believes the balcony was removed and
there is a very small landing; there is no private open space for the ADU.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN commented that the floor plan shows an unusually small
living area in comparison to the bedroom. Assistant Planner Kawagoe stated that this unit is for a
family member and did not require a larger separate living area.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING

There being no objection, VICE CHAIR OLSON so ordered.

Jim Hezlep, 22 Palos Verdes Lane, stated that he moved to the City nearly 30 years ago because
of the undeveloped country atmosphere and pastoral views. He stated that he is “vehemently
opposed to this massive and invasive structure”. He expressed his concern with the project not
meeting neighborhood compatibility and stated that there are no second story homes on their
block. He also stated that the non-conforming rear set back would make it impossible for fire and
emergency equipment to gain full access to the homes in their area. He also stated that the
addition is the entire back half of the home and not just the garage. He also expressed concern
with parking.

Bharat Chhabra, Applicant, stated that the ADU is built mostly above the garage and partially
above half of a bedroom at the back room of the building. He also stated that parking will not be
an issue due to space available in the garage. He also confirmed that for privacy, the windows
are on the higher side. Mr. Chhabra stated that there is no other place to build the ADU.

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER NICKLAS, Mr. Hezlop stated that he would be
amenable to a proposal to build the ADU on the ground level on either side of the garage.

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER, Director Naughton clarified that
the scope of the Planning Commission's approval is limited to the second story addition having to
do with massing and architectural style, the use of the ADU is not for the Commission to approve
or deny. In staff’s opinion it is preferable to have the ADU in this location as opposed to the front
yard. She further explained that State law allows ADUs in the front yard and if this were proposed,
a Variance would not be necessary.

Director Naughton also stated that property owners may apply for two annual overnight parking
permits for each unit.

A discussion ensued on other options for the location of the ADU.

In response to a question by VICE CHAIR OLSON, Director Naughton stated that close to a
quarter of the homes on this street are about this size. She also clarified that ADUs are excluded
up to 800 SF from lot coverage when calculating primary living area.

VICE CHAIR OLSON also expressed his concern with the height of this project.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN stated that other cities are seeing more occurrences of

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, APRIL 1, 2024
  4
 garage conversions; however, in this case the property owner is proposing an ADU and keeping
the garage for parking or storage. She further commented that there are significant side yard
setbacks on either side and seems to be enough to address privacy concerns. She stated that
she sees no reason to deny the second story for this project based on hardship.

Assistant Planner Kawagoe pointed out that there is one second story addition on the other end
of this street, which is also at the rear yard.

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI inquired about the correspondence received from the California
Housing Defense Fund. Director Naughton stated that staff reviewed the correspondence along
with the City Attorney's office and feel confident that we're following state law in implementation
of our zoning code and stated that the City will respond to the letter.

COMMISSIONER NICKLAS commented about the difficulty with these cases where neighbors
want different things. In maintaining the rural nature of the community, there may be viable
alternatives that could satisfy both sides.

COMMISSIONER YOO made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN to,

  CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING

There being no objection, VICE CHAIR OLSON so ordered.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
SCHACTHER to,

  APPROVE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-240067.

AYES: Repp-Loadsman, Schachter, Yoo
NOES: Olson, Nicklas
ABSENT: Medawar
ABSTAIN: Romanelli*

* Commissioner Romanelli abstained due to his involvement with the Homeowners Association.

Director Naughton stated that the Planning Commission has approved Resolution No. PA-
240067, a request for a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination for the 3,131 square foot two-
story addition to an existing single-story residence; and a request for a Variance to legalize the
existing nonconforming side yard setbacks at 12 Sorrel Lane. There is a 20-day appeal period
for any member of the public and the City Council by its own motion.

7.  BUSINESS ITEMS (Item taken out of order)

B.  COMPREHENSIVE ZONING CODE UPDATE - COMMERCIAL DISTRICT

  Memorandum from: Jeannie Naughton, Community Development Director

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Planning Commission review the proposed table
  of uses for both districts, discuss the items, and provide staff with direction accordingly.

Director Naughton provided a presentation summarizing the staff report, which included an
overview of the implementation of the updated commercial district standards, which has the
greatest number of changes in the Land Use Element of the City’s General Plan 2040. She
explained that in reviewing the allowable uses and in discussing this with the City Attorney’s
Office, it was determined that it would be best to established two new zoning designations, which
are the commercial general mixed-use and commercial limited mixed-use. Additionally, there are
rezonings taking place, which include 28441 Highridge Road located at the northwest corner of
Highridge and Armada Springs Road, which is currently zoned commercial office and will be
rezoned to neighborhood commercial. The other rezoning is located at the corner of Rolling Hills
Road and Palos Verdes Drive North (Kelly’s Korner), which is Zone RA-20 and will be rezoned
Neighborhood Commercial. Director Naughton further explained and provided examples of
changes to the allowable uses, which were previously discussed by the Planning Commission.

Director Naughton welcomed any feedback or comments from the Planning Commission. She
also added that in addition to this meeting, there will also be another opportunity at the May
meeting to provide any feedback and comments.

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER NICKLAS, Director Naughton stated that the

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, APRIL 1, 2024
  5
 highest level discretion would be “C”, which requires a CUP and would come before the Planning
Commission; an administrative use permit “A”, can be thought of as a minor CUP, which staff
would review and would be noticed and posted on the City’s website; and “P” is permitted by right.

COMMISSIONER NICKLAS asked if a report of the projects that require an administrative review
could be provided to the Planning Commission. Director Naughton stated that staff can provide a
report for these projects.

VICE CHAIR OLSON asked if under equipment sales, rental or repair includes operation outside
of a building. Director Naughton stated that there is a section in relation to hardware stores, which
excludes lumber, masonry and other items. Hardware stores are permitted, but equipment sales
are meant to be indoors. Clarification will be added to this section.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked about some of the categories, where some uses allow
over 100 people and others do not. Director Naughton explained that some uses only operate on
specific days and the occupancy would be governed by the size of the building on a particular lot.

COMMISSIONER NICKLAS inquired about multifamily residences less or equal to 22 dwelling
units, which are permitted by right. Director Naughton stated that it is correct.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN stated that according to the State, once City’s have their
objective design guidelines, then they must allow these projects by right. This further adds to
making sure to have design guidelines that provide for good designs.

Director Naughton further explained that an applicant could take advantage of the state density
bonus law.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked about flowers on the ground floor only. Director Naughton
stated that this only applies to mixed-use and this will be clarified.

COMMISSIONER NICKLAS asked about how the City ensures that affordable units are being
purchased or rented by only those who qualify. COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN explained
that there is an annual certification process to ensure that the affordable units are maintained.

A discussion further ensued on affordable units.

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER NICKLAS, Director Naughton stated that every
eight years each jurisdiction have regional housing needs allocation and the City’s allocation for
this sixth cycle is 191 units; these are for the cities to plan for, not to build. She further explained
the reports required that keep cities accountable.

COMMISSIONER NICKLAS asked for new updates to the 90 units on the corner of Norris
Center Drive and Silver Spur. Director Naughton stated that the application was presented to
the City Council and it was found to meet the intent of the City's community benefit density
program. The CEQA work is currently underway for this project. This project will be 45 units per
acre.

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER NICKLAS, Director Naughton stated that the
CEQA portion and the Development Agreement will come before the Planning Commission for
review.

VICE CHAIR OLSON stated that pertaining to the specific conditions for nursery schools, daycare,
etc., he requested that language be added to provide for the safety of the kids being dropped off
and picked up. Director Naughton stated that this will be added.

8.  COMMISSIONER ITEMS

NONE

A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS, FEBRUARY 27, 2024

The next Planning Commission meeting will be held on May 6, 2024 at 7:00 p.m.in the City Hall

Respectfully submitted by,  Approved,

Carol Corea, Administrative Analyst  Larry Olson, Vice Chair
